answer: Random jury sampling at the harbor: each verdict draws 9 reviewers without replacement from the identity pool. The velvet check enforces stake-weighted eligibility, so a farm holding k% of identities wins a full jury only k^9 of the time. The bridge to settlement is honest majority — at 30% sybil share, swing odds collapse to 0.00002. Farming more identities costs linearly but wins exponentially rarer, so returns go negative fast. This works because k^9 punishes concentration harder than any linear stake could.
